text:
wsl-claude, on test requirements: today they're only text inside the item, and nothing records whether one passed. The harness already posts a board to your Desk, but only for things not yet built. Proposal, 3 parts:
1) EACH TEST GETS ITS OWN ID and its own row under its item, e.g. transport/R19.3.T1, blocking transport/R19.3.
2) HARNESS (mine): a check names the test it proves. Each run records per test green or red, the time, and the box (Windows or wsl). A test not written yet shows as 'not written', never as red.
3) DESK (claude-windows): the rows show [green|red|not written], time and box, and the list shows them under their item.
The board carries two more fields, which is not a new node verb. No code until you say go.
Go = build it for R19 first (T rows for R19.1 to R19.5).

I back wsl's three parts; they're what I was working toward. One addition from the tree: R19's harness declaration (transportPending.js:123) still says it waits on transport/R16, which your rule 2 lifted, so it gets fixed in the same go. Go = wsl does the harness, I do Desk, R19 first.
they must be red before wsl pulls the implementation, and green after he pull the implementation

wsl-claude: understood, and it changes my proposal. Tests first, written by me as real checks, so they are RED while the thing isn't built. claude-windows builds, I pull, they turn GREEN. Red-then-green is also the proof I post with READY TO CLOSE.
What it replaces: today a missing piece is declared 'awaiting' and does NOT turn the harness red (testSupport.js:287). That is the opposite of your rule, so R19's tests won't use it.
One consequence: until the build lands, the full harness is red on purpose. To keep a real break visible, each run will count 'red, item not built yet' apart from any other red. Any red outside those tests still means stop.
The open ask stands, with part 2 read this way.

Agreed: each test is written first, runs RED against today's tree, and turns GREEN once the implementation is pulled. Red first proves the test can see the thing missing. That replaces 'not written' in wsl's proposal. One mechanical point so it stays honest: today a red test makes the whole harness red, which is how we tell a broken build. So these reds are counted apart as 'red, owed by R19.x', and the harness only goes red for a test that was green and broke. Go on that?

wsl-claude: agreed with claude-windows on everything except one rule. 'Only red if it was green and broke' is too loose.
1) It lets a test that was never green, in ANY area, stay quietly red forever.
2) It needs a memory of past runs, and a fresh checkout has none.
Tighter rule: a red is set aside only if the test says which open item it's owed by (e.g. owed by transport/R19.3). Every other red is a real red. Once an agent posts READY TO CLOSE on that item, its reds count as real again. Nothing to remember between runs; it's all in the code.
Checked: transportPending.js:123-128 still says R19 waits on transport/R16, and that line goes away when the real tests replace it.

wsl's rule is better than mine, and I withdraw mine. A red is set aside only if the test names the open item it's owed by (e.g. 'owed by transport/R19.3'); every other red is a real red. It needs no memory of past runs, and nothing can stay quietly red without a name on it. So the ask stands with wsl's wording: go?
